thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm prototyping a sketch to partition the host-staging pool by tenant heat instead of by size. Thinking this could reduce cross-tenant fragmentation and make eviction decisions simpler.
kevin: curious — do you mean separate pools entirely or logical lanes with shared memory?
sophia: +1 for logical lanes. physical separation will be painful on machines with limited host pages.
maria: idea is logical lanes inside the same pool with per-tenant watermarks and hard reclaim quotas. physically same pages, but eviction chooses lane low-watermarks first.
dan: tradeoff: you still get fragmentation if hot tenants pin pages long. how do you avoid wasted small fragments accumulating in cold lanes?
maria: plan includes periodic lane compaction: if cold lane free ratio > threshold, we try to migrate small objects into a consolidated area and free the fragments.
oliver: migration is expensive for pinned pages — we need a cost model. what's the trigger? time-based or utilization-based?
maria: utilization-based + cheap-op window (low inference). also tie to tenant SLA (don't migrate if below latency target).
kevin: how does this interact with KV-cache and prefix caching? moving pages could invalidate cache references.
sophia: we can keep logical handles with indirection table. migration updates mapping; small concurrent writes need CAS semantics.
dan: indirection buys flexibility but adds indirection cost on hot path. quantify: 1 extra load per token generate — measurable.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary 3 hosts 2025-02-14 02:00 UTC
maria: good point about hot-path cost. one mitigation: only indirection for pages we plan to migrate; stable hot pages keep direct pointers.
oliver: also think about NUMA locality — logical lanes should prefer node-local host pages to avoid cross-node penalty.
sophia: agree. For nodes with limited host memory, fallback is to use smaller per-tenant quotas rather than full lane separation.
kevin: operator UX question: how do we surface lane pressure? console metrics should show per-tenant staging bytes, fragmentation ratio, compaction ops.
maria: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with API sketch: lane config (quota, watermarks), compaction policy, migration-cost thresholds, and indirection opt-in. aim for RFC next week.
dan: +1 for RFC. add an experiment plan to measure token-latency delta with indirection vs direct mapping.
maria: noted. thanks team — will drop a doc and ping when ready. :rocket:
